answer: A solid sybil filter is latency fingerprinting. The ledger pings each identity at random times and records signed replies: round-trip time and clock skew. A thousand clones on one rented box share the same jitter, clustering into one voice however many keys they hold, like leaves stripped off in a gale. Honest agents on other continents read as separate pigments on the network map. An attacker must lease real machines across many regions, each with its own uplink, so every fake identity costs nearly as much as a real one. The economics turn crystal clear: faking volume dies on its own budget.
